subject: May inference scorecard: leadership readout + QBR action grid
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-26T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: May inference scorecard — leadership readout & QBR asks

Team,

Attached is the May inference scorecard (May_dashboard_v2.pdf) plus a one-page executive snapshot. High-level bullets:

- Latency: median generation time stable at 110ms, P95 jumped from 430ms -> 610ms week-over-week (notable in EU region).
- Cost: platform unit cost up ~9% month-over-month; primary contributor: small-batch interactive jobs and repeated cold starts for smaller models.
- Uptime: 99.96% — within SLA but saw two 12m blips (root cause: autoscaler slow ramp during region failover).
- Usage: overall tokens up 18%; top 3 accounts account for 46% of that increase (diff attached in qbr_prep_notes_table.csv).

Asks for the leadership readout / QBR: please confirm owners for the following by EOD Tuesday (2028-05-28):
1) Latency drilldown (by model family + region) — owner: ? (deliverable: latency_breakdown.csv)
2) Cost mitigation shortlist (short-term routings/caching + medium-term quantization plan) — owner: ?
3) Usage attribution & top-customer appendix for QBR slides — owner: ?

I've dropped proposed slide deck v3 to the drive (link below) and attached the dashboard PDF. Quick prep call scheduled for Tue 2028-05-29 10:00-10:30 PT (calendar invite to follow).

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: May_dashboard_v2.pdf

Thanks Hannah — quick read, high priority on the latency side. A few notes:

- I can own the latency drilldown. I'll need raw tail samples and KV cache hit rates for the time window 2028-05-18 -> 2028-05-25.
- Ask infra to provide: per-model-family P50/P95/P99, per-region. Also include average request size and small-batch ratio; those are likely inflating the P95.
- I opened a short ticket SP-542 to track the investigation (link: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/SP-542). Please attach the dashboard PDF there.

Deliverable: latency_breakdown.csv (first pass) by EOD Monday (2028-05-28). If we see KV hit-rate < 75% for interactive requests, we should propose an aggressive cache-priming fallback for the QBR.

-Markus

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Hannah / Laura / Markus — quick update from usage side.

- I pulled request logs for the May 18-25 window. The significant token spike is driven by a scheduled nightly batch run from Nebula Analytics (ops-cust@nebula.io) that increased embedding calls and small-model classification traffic. The run ramped up after a config change in their pipeline; support already has the ticket (SUP-1829).
- Attached a short table (included in qbr_prep_notes_table.csv) with per-customer delta and the time-of-day pattern — the pattern matches the P95 latency spikes (nightly warm-up + bursty traffic).

Suggested immediate mitigations (for discussion in prep call):
1) Apply a soft throttle on Nebula's non-critical pipeline for 48 hours and move them to a dedup-enabled route.
2) Add a cache-prime on our warm-up window for the models they're hitting the most.

If Nebula ops @ ops-cust can confirm that the run is non-blocking, we can proceed with a temporary routing change and reflect savings in the QBR.

- Jonas
Director, Platform Analytics
Redwood Inference
